Performance was close to YOLOv8m (0.5033 mAP@0.5), while inference time remained lower at 4.5 ms per image. Freezing layers may therefore provide a useful balance between detection performance and inference speed. Performance was still improving at the end of training.

hypothesis: Higher resolution helps tiny defects (Finding 1) but costs time and memory
hyperparameters: weights=yolov8s.pt imgsz=960 batch=2 optimizer=AdamW lr0=0.001 run_name=E09
what_was_learned: Increasing the input resolution from 640 to 960 achieved a validation mAP@0.5 of 0.4652 and mAP@0.5:0.95 of approximately 0.2275. This was a small improvement over the initial E00 reference (0.4596 and 0.2108, respectively). However, inference time increased from 4.5 ms to 9.2 ms per image. The higher resolution therefore provided a modest improvement in detection performance at a higher computational cost. Performance was still improving at the end of training.
